subject: PD brief 29 Sep – 6 Oct 2026: 33 papers, 3 to dig into

synthesis.intro: These 8 days leaned heavily on resuscitation, trauma and stroke, with a steady stream of registry and systematic-review evidence that mostly supports or questions what we already do rather than demanding change. Standouts for the road: preoxygenation technique, paediatric dosing deviations, and warning signs before paediatric cardiac arrest.
synthesis.discussion: Half of the paediatric arrest survivors had prior warning symptoms that no one followed up — what is our realistic role, on an ordinary day job, in picking up and escalating those quiet red flags?

lessons.text: Flush-rate oxygen clearly outperformed a standard non-rebreather plus nasal cannula for preoxygenation in volunteers — a prompt to check your own preoxygenation setup before a planned airway.

Nearly half of paediatric medication doses in one quality registry deviated from protocol, mostly underdoses, with intranasal routes worst — worth double-checking your concentration and volume assumptions on the next paediatric job.

Half of paediatric cardiac arrest survivors had warning symptoms beforehand, often exertional syncope that was never followed up — treat paediatric exertional syncope as a genuine red flag and convey or refer with that concern documented.

A meta-analysis found no prehospital whole-blood mortality benefit, and observational work on trauma vasopressors remains conflicting and low certainty — a reminder that enthusiasm for new trauma therapies should stay grounded until randomised evidence firms up.
Methoxyflurane achieved meaningful pain score drops with 95% protocol compliance and no serious adverse events in a Canadian trauma cohort — reassuring for a drug many of us use routinely on scene.

deep_dives.topic: Timing and adjuncts in cardiac arrest
deep_dives.why: Several papers this period touched on what we do in the first minutes of arrest: drug timing, airway timing and what actually degrades our performance. The timing findings are retrospective and fragile, so they suit discussion rather than change.
questions: When do you currently give adrenaline relative to your first advanced airway attempt, and does that match your local guideline?
Which of the described barriers — environmental, cognitive, team dynamics — do you recognise from your own difficult arrests?
deep_dives.ideas: Compare the Korean registry's early-adrenaline-plus-early-airway signal with its own sensitivity analyses, and ask whether the interaction would survive the time biases you see in real arrests. Look at what the economic review says about early defibrillation and termination-of-resuscitation rules against your local guideline's criteria.

deep_dives.topic: Stroke chains that break before us
deep_dives.why: Stroke papers this period spanned patient delay, First Nations assessment gaps and AI triage — all stages upstream of thrombectomy. Together they show the biggest losses happen before or around our assessment.
questions: How would you recognise and counter patient-side delay on a stroke call in your community?
Do you complete a formal stroke assessment on every suspicious presentation, and what gets in the way?
deep_dives.ideas: Compare the documented paramedic stroke assessment rate for First Nations patients (58.2%) with non-Indigenous patients (67.3%) and consider what explains the gap locally. Consider whether the AI triage model's high negative predictive value would actually change disposition decisions for patients you convey.

deep_dives.why: Whole blood, vasopressors, crew size and minithoracostomy all featured, with mostly weak or null evidence. This is a good hour to separate what we believe from what has been shown.
questions: How would you weigh a five-minute scene-time saving against uncertain survival benefit when choosing an intervention on a trapped trauma patient?
Does the finding that larger crews speed tasks but not survival change how you think about task allocation on your crew?
deep_dives.ideas: Compare how the minithoracostomy cohort and the crew-size registry define success — one counts complications and scene time, the other survival — and consider which outcome matters for your next chest trauma job. Ask whether the vasopressor evidence's confounding by indication makes any of its associations interpretable at all.

papers.title: No sex differences in OHCA with confirmed CAD
papers.design: Post hoc analysis of a prospective European OHCA registry
papers.n: 580 adults with OHCA and angiographically confirmed obstructive CAD (15.3% women)
papers.finding: 30-day survival 66.2% (women) vs 61.5% (men), p=0.33; favourable neurological outcome 55.1% vs 53.8%, p=0.82; sex not associated with 30-day survival (adjusted OR 0.75, 95% CI 0.39–1.41).

papers.title: Prehospital minithoracostomy vs chest drain
papers.design: Retrospective physician-led HEMS cohort with Bayesian analysis
papers.n: 94 major trauma adults (66 minithoracostomy, 28 chest drainage)
papers.finding: Posterior median scene-time difference −5.9 minutes (95% CrI −13.8 to 1.7); recorded complications 0/50 evaluable minithoracostomy vs 6/10 evaluable chest drainage (risk difference −58.7 percentage points, 95% CrI −83.9 to −29.3); no clear survival differences at 1, 30 or 90 days.

papers.title: NRB + nasal cannula inferior to flush-rate preoxygenation
papers.design: Experimental crossover study in healthy volunteers
papers.finding: Mean FeO2: flush-rate NRB 85% vs 68% (NRB + nasal cannula at 15 L/min each) and 75% (at 25 L/min each); differences of 16% (95% CI 13–20%) and 10% (95% CI 6–14%), both failing non-inferiority.

papers.title: Post-OHCA outcomes at Victorian Heart Hospital
papers.design: Retrospective audit of a dedicated cardiac hospital ED
papers.finding: Survival to discharge 50.4%; 30-day survival 40.0%; shockable rhythms 61.2%, prehospital ROSC 92.6%; shockable rhythm (OR 3.46), cardiac aetiology (OR 3.40) and prehospital ROSC (OR 9.23) associated with survival; 24.0% needed interhospital transfer.

papers.title: Paediatric non-transport re-call rates low
papers.design: Retrospective cross-sectional study of EMS data
papers.finding: 1% of non-transported children had a repeat 9-1-1 call with transport within 72 hours; 11 (0.1%) deaths on scene at re-call; of 1,001 with hospital-linked data, 89% ED discharge, 16% hospitalised, 0.2% died.

papers.title: Co-design of urine culture stewardship in ED
papers.design: Qualitative descriptive study using co-design workshops
papers.finding: Culture, complexity and efficiency drove low-value urine cultures; education, nudges, clinical champions and audit/feedback were selected as intervention components, with workflow inefficiency and credibility of change seen as challenges.

papers.title: AI triage of ED CT brain scans
papers.design: Retrospective validation study of an AI model
papers.n: 3,424 adult non-contrast ED CT brain scans
papers.finding: AI sensitivity 85.4% (95% CI 80.0–89.0%), specificity 69.1%, NPV 98.3%; post hoc re-adjudication gave sensitivity 94.3% and NPV 99.4%; ~64% of encounters potentially eligible for expedited disposition; no false negative required urgent intervention at index visit.

papers.title: PIHCA vs GO-FAR 2 for IHCA prediction
papers.design: External validation using Swedish Registry of Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation data across three hospitals
papers.finding: 28% survived with favourable neurological outcome; AUROC 0.73 (95% CI 0.67–0.78) for PIHCA vs 0.70 (95% CI 0.65–0.75) for GO-FAR 2, difference not significant; calibration adequate for both

papers.title: Prehospital whole blood no mortality benefit
papers.design: Systematic review and meta-analysis (random-effects) of RCTs and comparative cohorts
papers.n: 4,040 adult trauma patients (1,558 whole blood; 2,482 standard care) across 6 studies
papers.finding: No significant reduction in 24-hour mortality (RR 1.00, P=0.98) or 28/30-day mortality (RR 1.09, P=0.30); reduced 24-hour red cell requirements (MD -0.97, P=0.03) lost significance on sensitivity analysis

papers.title: Early adrenaline + early airway in OHCA
papers.design: Retrospective national registry cohort (Korea OHCA Registry)
papers.n: 20,662 adults with OHCA receiving prehospital adrenaline and advanced airway management
papers.finding: Early adrenaline (≤10 min) + early airway (≤6 min) vs late/late: good neurological recovery aOR 2.44 (95% CI 1.93–3.08), survival to discharge aOR 2.18 (95% CI 1.87–2.55); early airway with late adrenaline no benefit (aOR 0.99); interaction attenuated in sensitivity analyses

papers.title: Language barriers change trauma assessment
papers.design: Retrospective national EMS dataset analysis (ImageTrend, 2022–2023)
papers.n: 1,220,982 blunt trauma EMS activations (24,857 with documented language barrier)
papers.finding: Language-barrier patients more often treated and transported (80.3% vs 75.1%) but less likely to have pain scores documented (60.6% vs 63.6%), with slightly more GCS 3–8 presentations

papers.title: NAEMSP statement on EMS mental health
papers.design: Position statement and resource document
papers.finding: NAEMSP recommends organisational recognition of EMS clinician mental health, education inclusion, multi-faceted confidential support, quality improvement, and legislative advocacy

papers.title: Risk-score-guided conveyance safe in chest pain
papers.design: Pragmatic randomised open-label blinded-endpoint non-inferiority trial
papers.finding: PreHEART-guided conveyance non-inferior for 3-day unexpected serious adverse events (win ratio 1.01, 95% CI 0.89–1.16); non-conveyance rose to 34.6% vs 24.5%, 30-day emergency presentations fell (RR 0.88), costs −€345, and no deaths within 3 days among 1526 non-conveyed patients

papers.title: Stroke care gaps for First Nations patients
papers.design: Retrospective population-based data-linkage cohort
papers.finding: Age-standardised EMS attendance incidence 343 vs 144 per 100,000 person-years (IRR 2.38); paramedic stroke assessment 58.2% vs 67.3%; conveyance to thrombectomy-capable hospitals 24.4% vs 32.7%; adjusted 30- and 90-day mortality similar (HR 0.81 and 0.81)

papers.title: What OHCA care is worth paying for
papers.design: Systematic review of economic evaluations
papers.finding: Early defibrillation and EMT-delivered ALS cost-effective (ICERs £11,407–US$56,700 per QALY); prehospital ECPR more cost-effective than in-hospital ECPR (AU$27,323–44,000 per QALY); termination-of-resuscitation strategies cost-effective (US$110,554 saved per QALY lost in one estimate)

papers.title: Nearly half of paediatric doses off-protocol
papers.design: Retrospective quality-improvement registry cohort
papers.n: 386 medication administrations in 240 children across nine agencies
papers.finding: 46.4% of doses deviated ≥20% from recommended (79.9% underdoses); deviation was highest for ondansetron (85.3%) and via the intranasal route (69.7%); weight-estimation error was not associated

papers.title: Prehospital vasopressors in trauma unproven
papers.design: Systematic review of observational studies
papers.finding: Associations with mortality were mixed; one military study found significantly lower adjusted survival with vasopressors (aOR 0.32, 95% CI 0.18–0.56), and one study linked them to massive transfusion (aOR 4.97) and trauma-induced coagulopathy (aOR 3.05)

papers.title: Methoxyflurane feasibility confirmed in Canada
papers.design: Single-centre prospective observational feasibility study
papers.finding: Protocol compliance 95%; median NRS pain 8/10 pre-treatment to 5/10 post-treatment; side effects in 23%, mostly mild, with no serious methoxyflurane-related adverse events

papers.title: Bigger crews work faster, don't save more
papers.design: Retrospective nationwide registry cohort
papers.finding: ≥3-person crews: IV access in hypotensive patients aOR 1.47 (95% CI 1.31–1.66), scene time ≤10 min aOR 1.09, advanced airway borderline (aOR 1.13); survival to discharge unchanged after adjustment (aOR 1.00)

papers.title: EMS and ED disagree on paediatric asthma signs
papers.design: Prospective observational agreement study
papers.n: 295 children aged 2–18 at five paediatric EDs
papers.finding: Slight agreement for suprasternal retractions (κ 0.01–0.20), fair for tachypnoea and accessory muscle use (κ 0.21–0.40), and poor agreement (ICC 0–0.50) for breathlessness, work of breathing, hypoxia and wheeze characteristics

papers.title: Two-thirds of stroke patients delay seeking care
papers.design: Systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.finding: Pooled prehospital delay incidence 67.7% (95% CI 59.2–75.6%); 65.0% at the 2-hour cut-off and 77.2% at 3 hours

papers.title: Direct geriatric admission depends on geography
papers.design: Cross-sectional register-based study
papers.finding: 603 patients (7%) directly admitted to geriatric units; crude conveyance rates ranged 4–21% across service areas, with supply-side factors (proximity, ownership, bed numbers) explaining most between-area variation

papers.title: US racial gaps in trauma interventions
papers.design: Retrospective registry cohort
papers.finding: Prehospital intubation 7.9% in White vs 4.0% in Black patients; prehospital blood 4.4% in patients of other race vs 2.3% in Black patients; socially disadvantaged neighbourhoods were less likely to receive prehospital interventions

papers.title: TRiM peer support training feasible for first responders
papers.design: Single-service feasibility and acceptability study with pre/post surveys and follow-up
papers.n: 21 first responders who completed training (27 registered)
papers.finding: 90–94% rated the training highly relevant; significant pre-to-post improvements in perceived capability, referral knowledge, risk evaluation and boundary clarity (d = 0.60–1.37); formal TRiM use was minimal at both follow-ups

papers.title: Shift-worker nutrition evidence: thin for responders
papers.journal: Journal of Human Nutrition and Dietetics
papers.design: Systematic review (PROSPERO-registered) with narrative synthesis and first-responder subgroup analysis
papers.finding: Most included studies were crossover RCTs (49%) or observational (33%); 40% involved nursing and healthcare professionals and only 9% first responders such as firefighters and police

papers.title: Anaphylaxis knowledge gaps in prehospital crews
papers.journal: Iranian Journal of Allergy, Asthma, and Immunology
papers.design: Descriptive cross-sectional survey (21-item questionnaire)
papers.finding: 52.2% identified all three diagnostic criteria, 81.7% recognised adrenaline as first-line, 81.1% knew the intramuscular route, but only 52.2% knew correct patient positioning and 50.6% auto-injector use

papers.title: Online stroke education boosts EMS-seeking
papers.journal: Journal of Education and Health Promotion
papers.design: Randomised controlled trial
papers.finding: Versus control, the intervention group showed greater gains in warning-sign awareness (aOR 3.78, 95% CI 1.41-8.13), stroke knowledge (aOR 3.68, 95% CI 1.52-8.94) and EMS-seeking (aOR 3.33, 95% CI 1.44-7.69)

papers.title: What actually degrades CPR performance
papers.design: Qualitative (conventional content analysis, COREQ-reported)
papers.finding: A nested four-layer model: physical and environmental threats trigger cognitive and motivational barriers, which interact with psychological and ethical stressors and extend to socio-cognitive challenges beyond the hospital

papers.title: Stroke triage tools: cost-effective, hard to sustain
papers.journal: Journal of Evaluation in Clinical Practice
papers.design: Systematic review of health economic and implementation studies
papers.n: 31 studies (13 with health economic outcomes, 18 with implementation determinants)
papers.finding: Of 6,491 screened studies, 31 were included (14 mobile stroke units, 13 telemedicine); positive cost-effectiveness was reported in 11 studies, but evidence on sustained implementation was limited and barriers included innovation complexity, role delineation, workflow compatibility, IT infrastructure and costs

papers.title: How rare is a prehospital birth? Very
papers.design: Cross-sectional review of prehospital electronic patient care records
papers.n: 1,137,222 ambulance dispatches over 8 years in a region of 1.2 million people
papers.finding: 3,543 dispatches (0.31%) were childbirth-related; ambulance staff assisted 310 out-of-hospital deliveries (0.03% of all missions) and performed delaying obstetric manoeuvres in 10 further complex cases

papers.title: NOF fracture care runs on tacit knowledge
papers.design: Exploratory qualitative study — eight online focus groups with 21 registered paramedics, framework-method analysis
papers.finding: Four themes: balancing rapid assessment with diagnostic uncertainty; managing immediate care amid competing priorities; the strengths and limits of the existing knowledge base; and a call for clearer, evidence-informed guidance — participants relied on tacit knowledge, peer learning and accumulated experience

papers.title: Paediatric OHCA: half had warning symptoms
papers.design: Single-centre retrospective review of consecutive paediatric OHCA survivors at a UK tertiary referral centre (1996–2025)
papers.finding: 50.9% had prior cardiac symptoms (syncope 23.6%); 50% of arrests occurred on exertion; 72.4% were later diagnosed with an inherited cardiac condition, most commonly hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; of 13 children with prior syncope only three sought medical attention and none had follow-up arranged

papers.title: Tabletop MCI exercises: how they're run and measured
papers.design: Scoping review (PRISMA-ScR) of prehospital MCI tabletop exercises 2015–2026, outcomes classified by Kirkpatrick model
papers.finding: A preliminary three-tier 'TTX Design Spectrum' typology; most evaluation sat at Kirkpatrick levels 1–2 (participant learning), with an added level 2+ (applied learning) category — little assessment of applied performance or system outcomes
